results.content:
Guild is a vendor-neutral control plane for AI agents. It lets organizations deploy, govern, and observe every AI agent their teams run, regardless of the framework, model, or team that built it. Guild sits between the agents your engineers create and the systems those agents touch, unifying identity, credentials, permissions, and audit into one layer.

Guild is framework-neutral. Deploy and govern agents built with LangChain, CrewAI, Mastra, custom code, or any other framework. This is Guild's BYOA (Bring Your Own Agent) architecture: agents come from wherever your teams already build them, and Guild provides the runtime and control layer that runs them safely in production. Import any agent from any model or build new agents from scratch—all inside a unified vendor-neutral control plane that lets you connect the right tools for every use case.

You can’t improve what you can’t see. Guild makes it easy to monitor all your agents at once, with AI observability to identify and resolve issues, build audit trails, and improve trust over time.

Credentials are scoped with per-endpoint controls to limit access. LLM interactions are mediated, and human approval flows can be enforced as needed. Governance is built directly into the runtime.

results.title: As enterprises confront AI agent sprawl, xpander wants ...
results.content:
That widening gap is creating a market for infrastructure that sits above individual models and agents — handling execution, permissions, observability, memory, access to enterprise systems and lifecycle management without forcing developers to reconstruct those services for every new agent.

xpander.ai, a startup founded by three former AWS principal engineers, is the latest company trying to own that layer.

The company is making its enterprise AI agent platform generally available today, positioning it as a vendor-neutral control plane for building, running and governing agents across different models, agent frameworks and infrastructure environments. [...] The caveat is that xpander’s vendor neutrality does not eliminate dependency; it moves the dependency up the stack. Enterprises can swap models, frameworks and infrastructure underneath xpander, but xpander’s proprietary Universal Harness and control plane become the layer coordinating execution, governance, identity, memory and auditability.

That could create a new form of lock-in if those configurations and operational state are difficult to migrate to another control plane. xpander’s public documentation does not yet explain how portable that layer is if a customer terminates its enterprise license.

The company is also announcing a $7.5 million seed round led by Pico Venture Partners, with participation from Emerge Ventures, Samsung Next and SeedIL. [...] The requirement for persistent execution is not unique to xpander. Temporal has made long-running, failure-resistant workflows the core of its AI pitch, while LangSmith supports persistent agent deployment and production observability.

What xpander is attempting to combine is that runtime infrastructure with enterprise collaboration and governance into a single, portable, flexible, vendor-neutral control plane.

## Omni tests the harness thesis

The company is also making Omni, its prebuilt agent, generally available.
